Fernhill Cancer Centre, Kestrel Lane, Wexford Green WG4 7TL  Tel 01632 960 418

I reviewed Mr Harlow in clinic today with his wife. He was diagnosed in February this year after presenting with urinary frequency and back pain. His PSA fell from 86 to a nadir of 1.9 ng/mL on 12/6/23 on androgen deprivation with Enantone and six cycles of docetaxel.

Unfortunately his PSA has since risen on three consecutive readings: 3.4 ng/mL on 4/9/23, 6.8 ng/mL on 16/10/23 and 11.2 ng/mL on 20/11/23. He remains on Enantone. I note that no recent testosterone level is available.

A PSMA PET-CT on 14/11/23 showed new uptake in the right sixth rib and the sacrum, in addition to the known T9 and L2 lesions. There is no visceral disease. The pelvic nodes are smaller than on the CT of 21/2/23.
He reports mild aching in the lower back, managed with paracetamol, and some fatigue. He is fully independent and still walks his dog daily. I would estimate his ECOG performance status at 1.
On examination his weight was 82 kg and blood pressure 142/86. There was no spinal tenderness and no neurological deficit in the legs.

Retired electrician. Lives with his wife. Ex-smoker, stopped in 1998, 20 pack-years. Drinks around 10 units of alcohol a week.

Mr Harlow has castration-resistant disease progressing after docetaxel. We discussed enzalutamide and abiraterone, and he is interested in a clinical trial if one is suitable. I have requested a testosterone level and a repeat PSA before his next clinic visit on 8/1/24.
He is due his next Enantone injection on 29/1/24. Zoledronic acid was discussed but deferred pending a dental review.

Dr Rowan Penhallow
Consultant Medical Oncologist
